title: Regional SLA smoothing & contingency notes (week of 2026-04-05)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for the infrastructure team focused on smoothing observed SLA variance across regions over the next 2 weeks and finalizing short-term contingency steps for an upcoming holiday-week traffic spike. Drafted during the 2026-04-05 infra sync; notes, decisions and action items below.

Attendees (live): Maya C., Owen P., Lena R., Kai N., Priya S., (recorded: #infra-ops channel)

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- US-West and EU-Central showed 12–18% higher p95 latency last week vs baseline when CNTRL pool hit 85% sustained utilization.
- Root cause appears to be increased tail queuing from a mix of long-sequence RLHF eval traffic + smaller bursty chat traffic hitting a shared pool combination.
- Short-term mitigation: pin high-variance workloads to dedicated small pools, enable per-customer soft-quotas for bursty tenants, and flip on staged eviction policy trial (tiered-eviction v1) in eu-central only for 48 hours to collect telemetry.
- We need a rapid fallback plan if the prewarm/eviction trial regresses p50 or increases cost > 8% over baseline. Contingency checklist below.

Observed metrics and behavior (week over week):
- US-West GPU pool (g4a-large): avg utilization 72% -> 84% last week; p95 latency baseline 210ms -> 245ms (+17%).
- EU-Central GPU pool (g4a-medium): avg utilization 61% -> 80%; p95 latency baseline 230ms -> 272ms (+18%).
- APAC pools unchanged; low traffic shift (weekend experiment) actually reduced p95 by 4%.
- Tail length distribution: 9% of requests > 1024 tokens (RLHF evals) causing KV cache churn.
- Eviction events rose ~30% after autoscaler bump on 2026-04-01; correlation with sudden model-variant fallbacks seen in traces.

Hypothesis and reasoning: 
- Mixed workload (very long evals + many small chat calls) leads to inefficient batching and uneven KV cache pressure. The runtime currently spots this late and falls back to generic scheduling, causing queuing on busy nodes.
- Autoscaler thresholds and single shared pool for both RLHF-eval and chat are amplifying tail latency.

Planned short-term changes (next 48–72 hours):
1) Pool partitioning (heat-based): create two ephemeral subpools in EU-Central: 
   - eu-central-eval (pinned, 2 x g4a-small) for long-sequence eval traffic (tagged by route: /eval/*).
   - eu-central-chat (remaining capacity) for low-latency chat.
   Owner: Owen P. Target: 2026-04-07 06:00 UTC.

2) Staged eviction policy trial (tiered-eviction v1) in eu-central only: 
   - Trial window: 2026-04-07 06:00 – 2026-04-09 06:00 UTC.
   - Telemetry to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, eviction_count, cost delta, fallback rate.
   Owner: Kai N. Rollback condition: p95 > baseline + 10% or cost increase > 8%.

3) Soft per-customer burst quotas: throttle very bursty tenants to a soft limit with automated graceful degradation (429 with Retry-After vs hard kill).
   Owner: Priya S. Target: 2026-04-08.

4) Short-term pre-warm window scheduling for predictable eval jobs: coordinate with solutions-eng to schedule heavy eval queues into pre-warm slots (off-peak).
   Owner: Maya C. Coordinate: solutions-eng.

Instrumentation and telemetry additions (for this trial):
- Add an annotation to traces marking eviction-policy-enabled and pool-type to filter easily in Loki/Tempo. (Dev: github PR 918 referenced above).
- Export KV cache hit/miss rate per node to metrics surface.
- Add small synthetic canary that runs a 1k-token generation every 5m in each pool to track tail changes.
Owner: Lena R. ETA: 2026-04-07 (canary) + 2026-04-08 (KV metrics).

Contingency checklist (if trial regresses):
- Immediate rollback of tiered-eviction (Kai) -> flip policy off and revert to baseline policy.
- Re-merge pools and move eval back to larger pooled nodes until autoscaler tuning completed (Owen).
- Notify customer-success for any tenants hit by soft quotas and offer temporary dedicated capacity if SLA risk (Priya).
- Run emergency autoscaler dampening (increase scale-out aggressiveness, lower scale-in) for 2 hours to absorb the spike.

Risk / open questions (recorded from sync):
- Does creating pinned eval pools materially raise cost? (finance check required).
- Can some long-sequence eval routes be switched to a quantized model variant safely? Who signs off on quality regression? (product/research).
- Is the telemetry overhead (canary + KV metrics) going to add noise to capacity measurements? Need to baseline instrumentation noise.

Action items (owner / due):
- Owen P.: create pool partitioning change and rollout script; test in staging -> 2026-04-06 EOD.
- Kai N.: implement eviction-policy toggle + dashboard panels; prepare rollback playbook -> 2026-04-06 EOD.
- Lena R.: add KV cache metrics + canary -> 2026-04-07 morning.
- Priya S.: draft customer messaging + soft-quota config for top 10 bursty tenants -> 2026-04-07.
- Maya C.: coordinate with solutions-eng for eval rescheduling; run tabletop for contingency playbook -> 2026-04-06.

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider a heuristic that tracks per-connection long-sequence probability and routes those to eval pool automatically (ML classifier). Nice to have, not for this week.
- Could we offer a low-cost "background eval" prewarmed offering for internal teams to move heavy runs off production pools? Pilot idea.

References & links (quick):
- Incident traces: slack thread #infra-incidents 2026-04-02 -> contains spike trace images.
- PR with eviction policy: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/918
- Autoscaler tuning doc draft: confluence.redwood.com/display/INFRA/Autoscaler+Tuning+Draft

Next sync / decision point:
- Re-evaluate trial telemetry at 2026-04-09 infra sync (standup). If rollback needed, execute contingency checklist immediately and record a postmortem doc.

End of working note.

(If you have edits, add inline comments or update this doc — this is intentionally a lightweight working draft to enable fast iteration.)
